items.title: Chubby Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: That was with Charlie Barnet’s band. ... We were playing

ctx.x: Let me ask you about a couple of little things that I read and I often wondered if they could possibly be true. Something about Trummy Young hiding in your bass case?

Oh yeah. That was with Charlie Barnet’s band. This is true. We were playing, and backstage, we’re on stage, and backstage there are two guys with a vest, and they really looked like who they were. They were C-O-P-S. And Charlie went off the stage while the band was doing something, and he’s talking to them. Of course he was probably afraid somebody in the band was in trouble of some sort you know. And that’s beside the point. But at any rate, the next tune was “Mood Indigo.” And on account of that, all the lights…

items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: I had a contract with Chubby... I had both of them [Chubby Jackson and Oscar Pettiford]... we were playing the Orpheum Theater in Minneapolis, and Chubby came in... I said, 'How would you like to come with the band.'

ctx.x: Lou Fromm, drums. Killian, McGhee, Holland and Pettiford do not appear on camera, as white actors sat in their places. Okay, tell me the bass story.
Well, that -- well, first of all, about, "Jam Session," that was recorded all over the -- filmed all over the country, and then they sewed it together in Hollywood,

so I can imagine how disjointed -- I never saw it, but I can imagine how -- what a cross patched, messed up thing it must be. Some of it was done in New York, some was done in Hollywood, and then, you know, they just recorded and filmed segments and sewed it together afterwards. They wrote the story afterwards, I think, and fit in all these things. If there was a story. Oh, you asked about Pettiford.
